relevance.rationale: Pure Diophantine number theory: hypergeometric constructions giving irrationality of at least one zeta(odd) in explicit ranges, and delta(a) > 0.395 log a for the dimension of the Q-span of 1, zeta(3), ..., zeta(a). Nothing here is q-deformed, categorical, or knot-theoretic, so no QOU derivation consumes it. It is nevertheless a citable state-of-the-art for one named claim already in the corpus: rem:surreal-bounds-graded-mikusinski predicts a depth-3 surreal bound applies to 'Apery-style irrationality questions (Zagier 1986)', and rem:transcendental-accounting's zeta(3) row records 'irrationality (Apery 1978); transcendence open'. Both cite 1978/1986-era sources for a line of work whose current state is Rivoal/Zudilin. Scope note: this is a citation-quality improvement, not evidence for or against any QOU claim.

keyResults.statement: For every odd a >= 3, delta(a) > 0.395 log a, where delta(a) = dim_Q span{1, zeta(3), zeta(5), ..., zeta(a)}.
keyResults.useForFolio: Makes concrete what 'Apery-style irrationality questions' currently means quantitatively, so rem:surreal-bounds-graded-mikusinski's depth-3 prediction is stated against the real state of the art rather than against Apery 1978 alone. Purely a citation upgrade; it does not test the surreal-bound prediction.

proposedActions.rationale: rem:surreal-bounds-graded-mikusinski names 'Apery-style irrationality questions' with only Zagier 1986 attached; Zudilin 2001 (with Rivoal) is the current state of that programme.
